headline: Morocco has put artificial intelligence into the name of a government ministry, appointing Ahmed Rahhou as minister of AI, digital transformation and administrative reform.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a real cabinet change tied to a national AI plan, but the 'first-ever AI ministry' label is the outlet's and the targets are government goals.
importance_line: Moroccans could see more AI tools in public services, such as the Idarati assistant for administrative paperwork, but the targets are government goals, and the article says success depends on carrying out the plan and sustained investment.
summary: Morocco World News reports that King Mohammed VI appointed Ahmed Rahhou on 16 Oct 2026 as minister of artificial intelligence, digital transformation and administrative reform in the new government led by Fatima Zahra El Mansouri, bringing AI into the name of the ministry that handles digital policy. Rahhou inherits the Morocco AI 2030 roadmap, which targets about $10 billion (100 billion dirhams) in extra economic output, 50,000 jobs and AI training for 200,000 people by 2030, while the outlet notes that Africa as a whole faces obstacles, with a July 2026 International Monetary Fund report ranking Sub-Saharan Africa lowest on its AI Preparedness Index, and says success depends on carrying out the plan.
notes: The headline calls it a 'first-ever AI ministry', but the article's own text says AI is added to the name of the existing digital transformation and administrative reform ministry; the entry words it that way and the score was not raised.
